newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Namibian President Sam Nujoma has hailed the recently signed water sharing treaty between Bangladesh and India.
The government is planning to formulate a national policy for the unregistered english medium schools.
Coal imported from Meghalaya of India contains higher proportion of sulphur and has a severe effect on environment, a scientific survey said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, during a meeting with Namibian President Sam Nujoma in New Delhi on Friday, said Bangladesh was ready to send skilled mnapower to Namibia.
Police has unearthed an organised gang of smugglers dealing with gold and drugs.
A high-level- flag meeting between Bangladesh and India begins on Saturday to find out a permanent solution to problems over the frontier corridor of "Tinbigha".
Bangladesh is due to sign a new cooperation agreement with the European Union in April.
The government will soon crack down on unscrupulous manpower agents whose illegal exports resulted in deportation and ban on Bangladeshi workers by a number of labour importing nations.
